propositions: The parent-first cascade walk logic is duplicated between claim.py and transition.py, violating DRY and introducing maintenance risk when the cascade algorithm evolves.

The _CASCADING_EDGES decision table is correctly single-sourced in transition.py, but the walk (recursion, cycle guard, TOCTOU re-check, error re-wrap) appears twice, once hardcoded in claim.py for open→in_progress and once generalized in transition.py.

Consolidating the walk into a shared lifecycle_cascade.py module with injected resolve_parent and advance callbacks allows both claim and transition to use identical ancestor traversal logic while preserving their distinct write primitives and decision tables.

Three cascading edges exist—(open→in_progress), (closed→open), and (closed→in_progress)—but claim only expresses one; a parametrized test driven from _CASCADING_EDGES is required to prevent future edges being added without cascade coverage.
